- Adding capabilities maps (channel, application, orderer levels) to channel config protobuf
- Capabilities provider implementation in common/capabilities

- Enforcement: binary crashes if it doesn't support required capabilities
- Orderer enforcement that orderer capabilities are enabled before application capabilities
- Integration with peer and orderer startup/validation paths
- Testing

- Shim changes, handler changes
- Tests

This is moderate: maybe 8-12 days.

**U3: Video tutorial for adding orgs to running network** - This is a documentation/media task:
- Create diagram/slides
- Script the process
- Record video
- Edit and publish

technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Extend the channel configuration protobuf with three separate capabilities maps: /Channel (both orderer and peer must support), /Channel/Application (peer must support), and /Channel/Orderer (orderer must support), exactly as described in the specification.

U1: Introduce a single capability string "V1.1" in each of the three maps for this increment; future versions (e.g., "V1.2") will be modeled as supersets so consumers never perform version-based logic.

U1: Implement the capabilities logic in new provider packages under fabric/common/capabilities (channel.go, orderer.go, application.go), exposing the state of each capability key via a simple registry/lookup.

U1: Expose the framework to consuming code through OrdererCapabilities, ApplicationCapabilities, and ChannelCapabilities interfaces in fabric/common/channelconfig/api.go, with naturally named boolean methods (e.g., SetChannelModPolicyDuringCreate()) so callers are decoupled from capability internals.

U1: Enforcement is fail-fast per the v1.1 requirement: a binary (orderer or peer) that encounters an enabled capability it does not support crashes immediately; no graceful degradation is implemented.

U1: The orderer will enforce that the /Channel/Orderer V1.1 capability is enabled before allowing the /Channel/Application V1.1 capability to be set, preventing application admins from forking the chain during the initial v1.0->v1.1 upgrade.

U2: Read-your-writes is implemented in the ledger transaction simulator/query executor by checking the transaction's own write set before querying the committed state; it is exposed as a new opt-in shim API (stub.GetTrxState(key)) and default GetState semantics remain unchanged.
U5: Decouple MSP configuration behind interfaces (MSPConfig as an interface) and provide a programmatic API so channel config blocks can be constructed in code without the configtxgen YAML profile.

U6: Remove chaincode package singletons by refactoring to constructor-based dependency injection (chaincode support, handler, launcher/executor wiring), preserving behavior while making components individually instantiable and testable.
U7: Generate core.yaml and orderer.yaml in the integration test framework via Go templates rendered from the World configuration struct, replacing static config files.

U8: The new lifecycle implements a validation-parameters provider interface returning endorsement/validation info per chaincode; the special '_lifecycle' chaincode returns an automatically generated signature policy requiring endorsement by a majority of channel organizations.

U4: CouchDB query performance is measured with the existing performance harness (Caliper/PTE-style), covering rich queries and pagination at multiple data volumes, producing a documented latency/throughput report.
assumptions: All work is performed by a single developer; 1 workday = 8 productive hours; estimates are effort, not elapsed time, and exclude code review wait time and upstream community governance delays.
The existing Hyperledger Fabric v1.x Go codebase, build tooling, protobuf code generation, and CI infrastructure are available and working.
Estimates include design, implementation, unit tests, integration tests where stated, and reasonable rework from reviews; they exclude release management and long-term maintenance.
For U3, the target network topology for the demonstration is fixed (e.g., two existing orgs, adding one org with peer and CA), and a publishing channel for the video already exists.
For U4, an existing performance test tool is reused with only minor adaptation; no new benchmarking tool is developed, and CouchDB is the only state database in scope.
For U7, the integration test framework and its World configuration concept already exist; only the template-based generation of core.yaml and orderer.yaml is added.
For U8, the new chaincode lifecycle (FAB-13523) framework is in place; this story only adds the validation-parameters interface and the '_lifecycle' special case.
External references (Gerrit examples, design doc) are accessible and consistent with the specification; no clarification is needed.
No changes are required to SDK or CA components beyond what the stories state, and no production deployment/migration of a live network is part of this increment.
The scope is limited to the eight listed user stories plus minimal cross-cutting integration and documentation work.

activities.activity_name: Capabilities config schema and protobuf design (U1)
activities.activity_description: Design the capabilities map extension to channel config at channel, application, and orderer levels; update protobuf definitions and regenerate code.
Implement fabric/common/capabilities packages (channel.go, orderer.go, application.go) defining the V1.1 capability keys and lookup/registry logic.

activities.activity_name: Channel config integration and capability API interfaces (U1)
activities.activity_description: Parse and validate the capabilities maps in channelconfig and expose OrdererCapabilities, ApplicationCapabilities, and ChannelCapabilities interfaces in api.go.
Orderer crashes on unsupported orderer/channel capabilities; enforce that orderer-level V1.1 is enabled before application-level capability can be set during reconfiguration.
Peer crashes on unsupported application/channel capabilities at channel initialization/join and gates v1.1 validation semantics on the enabled capabilities.
Add capabilities to configtxgen sample profiles and ensure configtxlator displays the new config values.
Unit tests for providers, config parsing/validation, and orderer/peer enforcement logic including the ordering guard.

activities.activity_name: Capabilities integration and upgrade scenario tests (U1)
activities.activity_description: End-to-end tests of rolling binary upgrade followed by rolling channel reconfiguration, verifying v1.0 binaries crash and v1.1 semantics activate per channel.

activities.activity_name: Read-your-writes API design and shim extension (U2)
activities.activity_description: Design and add the opt-in GetTrxState(key) API to the chaincode shim and handler plumbing.
Implement read-your-writes semantics in the TxSimulator/query executor by serving keys from the transaction write set before committed state.
Unit tests plus an end-to-end chaincode test demonstrating access to keys written earlier in the same transaction.

activities.activity_name: Validate add-organization procedure and demo environment (U3)
activities.activity_description: Set up the demo network and dry-run the full procedure for adding an organization to a running network without downtime.
Create the introductory presentation-style diagram and the step-by-step narration script.
Screen-record the procedure with narration, edit, and publish the final video.
Define workloads: query types (rich queries, pagination), data volumes, and measurement metrics.
Stand up the Fabric network with CouchDB and adapt the existing performance harness for the defined query workloads.
Run the benchmark matrix and collect latency/throughput results.
Analyze results and produce the documented performance report for Fabric queries on CouchDB.
Convert MSPConfig into an interface so custom MSP configurations can be constructed programmatically.

activities.activity_name: Programmatic channel config block construction API (U5)
activities.activity_description: Provide a library-level API to build a channel config block in code without the configtxgen tool.

activities.activity_name: Config block construction tests and documentation (U5)
activities.activity_description: Unit tests verifying constructed blocks match configtxgen output, plus usage documentation.

activities.activity_name: Chaincode singleton inventory and refactoring design (U6)
activities.activity_description: Identify all chaincode singletons and define the dependency-injection refactoring plan.
Refactor chaincode support, handler, and launcher/executor wiring to remove singletons and inject dependencies via constructors.

activities.activity_name: Rework tests affected by singleton removal (U6)
activities.activity_description: Update and stabilize unit and integration tests impacted by the refactoring.
Define how World configuration values map to core.yaml and orderer.yaml templates.
Implement template-based generation of peer and orderer configuration files from World config values in the test framework.
Tests verifying generated configuration files match expected values for various World configurations.
Design the interface returning validation parameters (endorsement policy and related info) for a chaincode.

activities.activity_name: Validation parameters implementation for new lifecycle (U8)
activities.activity_description: Implement the interface in the new chaincode lifecycle to return validation parameters for deployed chaincodes.
Return validation info for the '_lifecycle' chaincode itself with an automatically generated majority-of-organizations signature endorsement policy.
Unit and integration tests covering normal chaincodes and the '_lifecycle' edge case.
Cross-story integration, full regression runs, and CI stabilization for the complete increment.
Developer and administrator documentation for the capabilities framework and the other code features (excluding the U3 video).
